name: Shot Types
description: Framing distance and extent of the scene. Entries describe what stays visible, including the contact points and supports needed to understand an activity.
entries: detail view: one task-relevant object fills the frame with the hands using it visible
head-and-shoulders view: faces and upper shoulders dominate when the activity does not require lower-body context
hands-and-workpiece view: the shared task fills the frame, with wrists and sleeves distinguishing participants
full-body pair view: both existing participants fit completely within the frame
ensemble view: the requested cast fits together with each participant separately readable
panoramic establishing view: the landscape extends broadly around a small but identifiable main activity
vertical full-length view: the frame follows the subjects from overhead space to their supporting surface
square medium view: the main activity sits within a balanced frame with nearby context on every side
object-and-user view: a whole device and the participant using it share the frame
room-wide view: the room boundaries and the main subjects' positions within them remain visible
threshold view: both sides of a doorway and the activity at the opening fit within the frame
ground-contact view: the lower bodies and supporting terrain dominate when foot placement is the action's focus
close view: the main subjects fill most of the frame, with the contact points and details needed to understand their action still visible
middle view: the main subjects from their middle up, widening or lowering the frame when their hands, supports or lower-body action must be visible
full view: every main subject whole in the frame, from its top to where it rests on the ground, with space around it
distant view: the main subjects small within a wide place, the surroundings filling most of the frame
shared close view: the main subjects' faces and interacting hands share the frame, with enough surrounding context to distinguish who does what
knee-up view: the main subjects are shown from above their heads to below their knees, retaining the spacing between their bodies
environmental view: the main subjects occupy a readable part of the frame while the surrounding workspace or terrain explains the activity
wide horizontal view: the frame extends to either side of the main subjects, keeping their lateral relationships and the nearby space visible
